newsitem.title: USA: Exel to acquire two insurance groups.
newsitem.headline: Exel to acquire two insurance groups.

text.p: EXEL Ltd said on Wednesday its X.L. Insurance subsidiary has agreed to acquire the assets of two insurance organizations to grow its core business.
X.L. Insurance will acquire the assets of the American Excess Insurance Association, based in Farmington, Conn., effective immediately, the company said.
American Excess Insurance is an association of 13 major U.S. based insurance companies, EXEL said.

American Excess Insurance specializes in providing up to $100 million in excess third party liability coverage over a minimum attachment point of $25 million, the company said. The group's 1995 annual premiums were $47 million, the company said.
X.L. has entered a tentative deal to acquire all of the outstanding shares of Railroad Association Insurance Ltd, a mutual insurance company owned by 12 transportation companies, EXEL said.
Under the terms of this transaction, X.L. will provide insurance coverage to Railroad Association members for three years and will assume liability for known and unknown losses, EXEL said.
X.L. will receive approximately $50 million in loss reserves, premiums and fees as a result of this transaction, which is expected to be completed within the next 30 days, EXEL said.
Terms of the deals were not immediately available.
